headline: Computational methods resolve cell-cell communication and spatial expression context
label: Spatial Transcriptomics Computational Methods
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair deep learning, empirical Bayes and optimal transport with spatial and single-cell transcriptomic data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference that links spatially resolved or single-cell transcriptomes to cell-cell interactions, missing modalities, or cell state. Several items couple expression to spatial context: PACE uses hierarchical empirical Bayes to quantify cell-type-resolved proximity effects, SPADE combines a VAE, Gaussian mixtures and conformal prediction to flag spatially aberrant epithelial spots, and SPCC maps unpaired single-cell data onto spatial transcriptomics using an adversarial joint-VAE and Random Forest. Cell-cell communication is addressed by scRICH, which links its heterogeneity to RNA splicing, and by a review of 33 spatial methods for this inference. SpatialMOC and PENNE extend coverage by predicting missing modalities, from cross-modality representation learning and from live-cell images respectively. The common emphasis is inferring unmeasured or context-dependent expression from indirect measurements. scDECIPHER and OneCell CUT&Tag address regulatory logic and chromatin-transcriptome co-profiling, so the set is heterogeneous.
